patients.summary: Warehouse associate in his thirties with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, resistant hypertension and albuminuric CKD stage 1 who joins in 2020. Antipsychotic weight gain and insulin resistance, a left adrenal pheochromocytoma resected in 2022, pseudogynecomastia, tinea pedis and corporis, an oculogyric crisis after a risperidone increase, an ED migraine and phenazopyridine methemoglobinemia follow.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31M, new to us. Was followed at a community health center nearby for years; switching because his shifts make their hours hard and he wants to be able to text when something comes up.

Problems he brings:
- Schizophrenia. Followed by a community psychiatry clinic, sees his psychiatrist every couple of months. On olanzapine 10 mg at night. Says he has been steady, no admissions in years, working full time.
- Type 2 diabetes. On metformin 1000 twice a day. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, usually 120s-140s.
- Hypertension. Three drugs: amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atenolol 50. Told by his old office his pressure was 'stubborn.' Takes them every day, uses a pill box.
- Kidneys: old office told him he has protein in his urine and early kidney disease. Creatinine normal per him. Will confirm with records.

Allergies: none known.
Meds as above.
Surgeries: none.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes, mother with high blood pressure, an uncle on his mother's side with schizophrenia.
Social: warehouse associate, day shift, lot of lifting and walking. Never smoked. Drinks socially, a few beers on a weekend. No drugs.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no headaches, no vision change, no urinary symptoms. Mood okay.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pleasant, a little quiet, good eye contact. HEENT unremarkable, neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities no edema, feet with intact monofilament sensation and good pulses. Skin clear.

A/P
1. T2DM: continue metformin. A1c, CMP, lipids, urine albumin/creatinine today.
2. HTN on three agents: BP above goal today. Continue current regimen for now, get records, recheck in 3 months.
3. CKD stage 1 by albuminuria per history: urine ACR today.
4. Schizophrenia: stable with outside psychiatry. Will do his metabolic labs here and copy psychiatry.
5. Health maintenance: flu shot today. Hep C screen today. Records release signed.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jorge, your labs from Wednesday are in. A1c 6.6, which is decent control on the metformin. Kidney function (creatinine) is normal. The urine protein test shows a small amount of albumin, matching what your old office told you, and we'll follow it every year. Cholesterol and blood counts as attached. Hep C screen negative. Nothing to change right now. See you in December.

Medications match our list: olanzapine 10 mg qhs, metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atenolol 50 mg. No known drug allergies. Immunizations: Tdap 06/2011, yearly flu shots. Labs over the last several years with normal creatinine and urine albumin above normal on repeat testing. Normal CBCs.

documents.body:
Annual exam, fasting.

Interval: fine since April. Both covid shots in the spring. Psychiatry unchanged, still olanzapine 10 at night, feels 'level.' Work steady. No ER visits.

Meds: olanzapine 10 qhs, metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atenolol 50. No drug allergies.
Social: never smoker, a few drinks on weekends, no drugs. Lives in Chicopee, works warehouse day shift.
Family: unchanged.

Exam

HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx normal, no thyromegaly.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, NT, no masses.
Ext: no edema.
Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.
Skin: no rashes.
Psych: calm, linear, appropriate.

Assessment / plan
- Type 2 diabetes: fasting labs today (A1c, CMP, ACR). Eye exam done in July, no retinopathy. Foot exam normal.
- Hypertension: 134/86, continue three-drug regimen.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up (missed January).

He has put on 15 lb in about six months and doesn't know why - says he eats the same and is as active as ever at work. Over the same stretch he has been more thirsty and getting up at night to pee, sometimes twice. No dysuria. No blurry vision. Mood and thinking steady; still olanzapine 10 at night and has been doing well on it for well over a year.

Meds: olanzapine 10 qhs, metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atenolol 50. NKDA.

BP 135/85. Weight 88.8 kg, BMI 30.
Exam unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema, skin clear.

Fasting labs 4/13: glucose 126, A1c 7.2 (was 6.5-6.8 all of last year). Lipids: TC 220, LDL 140, HDL 35, TG 250. Urine ACR 86.

A/P
1. Type 2 DM, worse: A1c up to 7.2 with weight gain, polydipsia and nocturia. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Diet review, handout given, he will cut the sugary drinks he admits to on night shifts.
2. Insulin resistance: weight gain, low HDL, high TG and rising glucose on olanzapine. The pattern fits the drug. Writing to his psychiatrist to ask whether a more weight-neutral antipsychotic is reasonable; not changing anything psych-related myself.
3. Obesity, new as of today, BMI 30.
4. HTN: 135/85 on three drugs, continue.
5. CKD 1: ACR 86, creatinine normal last fall.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Letter to psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw our mutual patient Jorge Reyes today. Over the past six months he has gained about 15 lb and his diabetes has worsened, A1c 7.2 from a previous range of 6.5-6.8, with HDL 35 and triglycerides 250. His psychiatric symptoms remain well controlled on olanzapine 10 mg nightly, which I know matters a great deal.

Given the metabolic picture, would you consider whether an agent with less weight and glucose effect would be appropriate for him? I will keep following his weight, A1c and lipids here and am glad to send results whenever useful.

Thank you,
Primary care physician

Thank you for your letter about his metabolic changes. We discussed options with him at his visit on 05/09/2022. He remains stable today. We would welcome repeat glucose and lipids at your next visit.

Community psychiatry clinic

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning asking to be seen for 'attacks.' Since around the beginning of July he gets spells of pounding headache, drenching sweat and his heart racing, a few times a week, lasting maybe 15-30 minutes. Some of them come with a feeling that something terrible is about to happen. Between spells he feels okay. Not tied to meals or exertion. No chest pain, no syncope. Says these do not feel like his old psychiatric symptoms. Switched to risperidone in May, otherwise no med changes, no caffeine pills or decongestants, no drugs.

BP 158/98 (recheck 156/96), HR 96 - higher than usual for him on atenolol. Afebrile. Weight 91.5.
Anxious-appearing but calm. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, slightly fast, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No tremor. Skin warm.

A/P
Paroxysmal headache, sweating, palpitations with worsening BP in a young man already on three antihypertensives: need to rule out pheochromocytoma. Also thyroid. Plasma free metanephrines and TSH today, A1c while drawing. Not changing BP meds today. He will text if a spell is severe or lasts longer. Will call with results.

orders.reason: Elevated plasma metanephrines, paroxysmal symptoms, resistant hypertension

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. TSH normal. Plasma free metanephrine 470 and normetanephrine 1450 pg/mL, both well above range. Explained this can point to an adrenal tumor that releases adrenaline-type hormones, and we need to confirm. Ordering 24-hour urine collection (jug and instructions at front desk) and an urgent endocrinology referral. A1c 7.0. Told him to keep taking all BP meds, avoid decongestants, and go to the ED for a spell with chest pain, severe headache that won't quit, or fainting. He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: 24-hour urine drop-off
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt dropped off 24-hour urine collection, started 8/22 0730 and finished 8/23 0730 per his log. Kept on ice. Sent to lab.

orders.order: MRI adrenal with and without contrast

documents.title: 24-hour urine result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 24-hr urine metanephrines and normetanephrines both clearly elevated, consistent with the blood test. Discussed with pt. Ordered MRI abdomen (adrenal protocol) so endocrinology has imaging at the consult. Endo appointment confirmed for 9/30; asked their office to call if anything opens sooner. Spells unchanged, no ED visits.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI ABDOMEN WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST, ADRENAL PROTOCOL

Indication: Elevated plasma and urine metanephrines.
Comparison: None.
Technique: Multiplanar multisequence imaging of the abdomen before and after IV gadolinium.

Findings:
Adrenals: 3.0 cm mass in the left adrenal gland. The right adrenal gland is normal.
Kidneys: Normal size and enhancement bilaterally. No hydronephrosis.
Liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas: Normal.
Vessels: No aortic aneurysm.
Lymph nodes: No adenopathy.
Bones and soft tissues: Unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 3.0 cm left adrenal mass. Otherwise normal MRI of the abdomen.

documents.title: MRI result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed MRI with Jorge by phone: 3 cm left adrenal mass, everything else normal. With the lab results this very likely explains the spells and his hard-to-control BP. Usually treated by removing the gland after medication prep, which endocrinology will set up. He was relieved there's an explanation. Sent MRI report to endocrinology ahead of 9/30.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology consultation
Referred by: primary care
Reason: elevated metanephrines and adrenal mass

History: 33-year-old man seen for three months of spells of headache, heavy sweating and palpitations. They come in discrete episodes, and he describes some as carrying a sense of dread, as though something bad is about to happen. Since his primary care visit in April his blood pressure has been difficult to control even though he reliably takes amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide and atenolol. Other history: schizophrenia on risperidone through his psychiatrist, type 2 diabetes on metformin, CKD stage 1, obesity, insulin resistance. NKDA. Never smoker, social alcohol, warehouse work. Father with diabetes, mother with hypertension, maternal uncle with schizophrenia.

Exam: BP 160/100, HR 98. Alert, comfortable. Thyroid normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdominal bruit is audible. No edema.

Data: plasma free metanephrines from primary care elevated. 24-hour urine metanephrines and normetanephrines elevated. MRI abdomen: 3 cm left adrenal mass. Today: Na 140, K 3.2, glucose 98. Aldosterone and renin sent given the low potassium.

Impression: Pheochromocytoma, left adrenal, biochemically and anatomically consistent.

Plan:
1. Start phenoxybenzamine 10 mg twice daily for alpha blockade before surgery; liberal salt and fluids. Continue his other antihypertensives. Atenolol may stay now that alpha blockade is starting.
2. Referral to endocrine surgery for laparoscopic left adrenalectomy.
3. Potassium is 3.2 on hydrochlorothiazide; please replete through your office.
4. Aldosterone/renin pending.
5. After surgery we will repeat metanephrines and discuss genetic testing.

Thank you for this referral.
Endocrinology

documents.author: general surgery

Endocrine surgery clinic

Seen for a 3.0 cm left adrenal pheochromocytoma referred by endocrinology. On phenoxybenzamine 10 mg BID since 9/30 with good blood pressure response and fewer spells. Never had abdominal surgery. NKDA. Exam: abdomen soft, nontender, no scars.

Plan: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy, scheduled 11/17/2022. Continue phenoxybenzamine through the morning before surgery. Expect 1-2 night stay. Risks, benefits and alternatives reviewed; consent signed.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Left adrenal gland, laparoscopic adrenalectomy.

GROSS: Adrenal gland with an attached well-circumscribed tan-brown nodule measuring 3.0 cm in greatest dimension.

MICROSCOPIC: Nested neoplasm of polygonal cells with granular cytoplasm, consistent with pheochromocytoma. The tumor is confined to the adrenal gland. Margins are negative. Uninvolved adrenal cortex is unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Left adrenal gland: pheochromocytoma, 3.0 cm, confined to the adrenal gland; margins negative.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admission 11/17/2022 - discharge 11/19/2022
Procedure: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy, 11/17/2022, uncomplicated.
Indication: left adrenal pheochromocytoma, prepared with phenoxybenzamine.

Course: Tolerated surgery well. Blood pressure stable in the low 120s-130s systolic after surgery; glucose monitored and managed with his usual metformin once eating. Ambulating, tolerating diet, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Port sites healing.

Discharge medications: STOP phenoxybenzamine. Continue amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atenolol 50 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, risperidone 2 mg BID. Acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks; endocrinology in 6-8 weeks with repeat metanephrines; surgery clinic in 3 weeks. Final pathology to follow.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 9 days after laparoscopic L adrenalectomy. Pathology came back: 3.0 cm pheochromocytoma, confined to the gland, clean margins.
Feels good. No more spells since surgery. Port sites a little sore, using acetaminophen once a day. Eating well, bowels normal. Back to light duty next week per surgery.

BP 132/84 off phenoxybenzamine, on amlodipine/HCTZ/atenolol. Afebrile.
Incisions: four small port sites healing, no redness or drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near ports. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P
- s/p L adrenalectomy for pheo: doing well. Endocrinology in January with repeat metanephrines.
- HTN: continue all three meds; reassess over the next months now that the tumor is out.
- DM2: metformin; A1c in January.
- Work note for light duty given.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up, 8 weeks after laparoscopic left adrenalectomy.

No spells since surgery. Recovered well, back at full duty at the warehouse. Taking amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atenolol, metformin and risperidone. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Healed port sites. Heart regular.

Pathology: pheochromocytoma 3.0 cm, confined to the gland, negative margins.

Results: plasma free metanephrine 39 and normetanephrine 92 pg/mL, both normal. Biochemical cure.

Plan:
1. Pheochromocytoma resected and biochemically cured.
2. All patients with pheochromocytoma are offered germline genetic testing; he agreed, sample sent today. We will send the result.
3. Yearly plasma metanephrines for surveillance.
4. Blood pressure management continues with primary care.

Endocrinology

documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Germline multigene panel for hereditary pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant detected. Result reviewed with the patient by phone. Plan unchanged: plasma metanephrines yearly, next due January 2024.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology new patient visit

34-year-old man referred by primary care. History of schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes and obesity; recently evaluated by his PCP for pseudogynecomastia.

Several months of itching and peeling between his toes. It came on gradually and goes up and down despite over-the-counter creams. Worse when he wears his tight work shoes for long shifts; better on weekends when he is barefoot at home. At work he uses shared locker rooms and showers, and a few coworkers have had the same thing. No fever, joint pains or other systemic symptoms.

Medications: risperidone, metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atenolol 50 mg. NKDA.

Exam: Both feet show peeling and scaling in the interdigital web spaces. No vesicles, no cellulitis. Remainder of the exposed skin is clear.

Procedure: scraping taken from the web spaces for KOH preparation and fungal culture.

Assessment: tinea pedis (interdigital), clinically.

Plan: ketoconazole 2% cream twice daily for 4 weeks to the web spaces, continuing a week past clearing. Dry thoroughly between toes, moisture-wicking socks, rotate work shoes, and wear sandals in the shared showers. We will send the KOH and culture results.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE

CC: eyes rolling up, neck twisting

HPI: 35-year-old man with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, CKD and obesity, followed regularly by his PCP (history includes insulin resistance, a resected pheochromocytoma, pseudogynecomastia and tinea infections). His psychiatrist increased his risperidone four days ago. Today he has had several sudden spells in which both eyes lock upward, each lasting as long as an hour, with his neck and trunk pulled into a twisted posture. Between spells he is awake, alert and without fever. No eye injury or eye surgery. Denies seeing things that aren't there and denies any change in his vision.

Medications: risperidone (dose recently raised), metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atenolol 50 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
SH: never smoker, social alcohol, warehouse associate.
Family: schizophrenia in maternal uncle, diabetes in father, hypertension in mother.

Exam: Vitals as recorded, afebrile. During an episode: sustained upward gaze of both eyes with torticollis. Face without rash; conjunctivae not injected; no eyelid swelling. Between spasms neurologic exam is otherwise normal - no tremor, no clonus, no rigidity.

ED course: Benztropine 2 mg IV at 20:05; episode resolved within about 20 minutes and none recurred during 3 hours of observation.

Impression: Oculogyric crisis - acute dystonic reaction to recent risperidone dose increase.

Disposition: Discharged home. Benztropine 1 mg by mouth twice daily for 7 days. Call psychiatry tomorrow regarding the dose. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for recurrence not relieved by benztropine, fever, stiffness or confusion.

events.reason: Shortness of breath, blue lips and fingers

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY MEDICINE NOTE

CC: short of breath, lips and fingers blue

HPI: 36-year-old man with schizophrenia and CKD, previously seen in this ED for an oculogyric crisis and for migraine. Two hours ago, after taking the medicines his PCP prescribed this morning for a new urinary tract infection (ciprofloxacin and phenazopyridine), he became suddenly short of breath and noticed his lips and fingertips turning blue. He felt fine before taking them.

PMH: schizophrenia, DM2, HTN, CKD, obesity, s/p left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma, migraine.
Meds: risperidone 3 mg BID, metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atenolol 50 mg; ciprofloxacin and phenazopyridine started today.
Allergies: NKDA on file.
Social hx: never smoker, social alcohol, warehouse associate.

Exam: RR 28, SpO2 85% on room air and unchanged on 100% oxygen by non-rebreather. Anxious. Central and peripheral cyanosis. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

ABG on 100% O2: PaO2 98 mmHg, PaCO2 38 mmHg, methemoglobin 15%. CBC, electrolytes and renal function within normal limits.

Assessment: acquired methemoglobinemia, symptomatic, from phenazopyridine.

ED course: phenazopyridine discontinued. Methylene blue 1 mg/kg IV over 5 minutes at 14:20. Repeat co-oximetry at 15:15: methemoglobin 2.1%. SpO2 97% on room air by 15:20, cyanosis cleared, breathing comfortably. Observed until evening without recurrence.

Disposition: home. Do NOT take phenazopyridine again - added to allergy list here; please update primary care record. Continue ciprofloxacin as prescribed. PCP follow-up in 2-3 days. Return for any recurrence of blue color or breathlessness.

documents.title: Urine culture result
documents.author: PCP
